title: Mixed Conditionals: Past Policy, Present Markets

sections.content:
You know mixed conditionals with *si* + *hubiera* and the simple conditional from B2 Unit 11. Economic analysts use this structure constantly to judge past decisions by their present consequences: a policy that was or was not adopted in the past is linked to how prices, credit or budgets stand today.

The *si* clause takes the pluperfect subjunctive (*hubiera* or *hubiese* + past participle) for the unreal past action. The main clause takes the simple conditional (*sería*, *tendría*, *habría*)—not *habría* + participle—because the result holds in the present, often marked by *hoy*, *ahora* or *actualmente*. If both cause and result belong strictly to the past, use the past-past pattern from B1 Unit 35 (*habría* + participle in the result).

sections.title: Past cause, present vs past result
rows: Present result: si + hubiera/hubiese + participle, simple conditional
Si el banco central hubiera subido las tasas a tiempo, hoy la inflación sería menor.
Present result: si + hubiera/hubiese + participle, simple conditional
Si el gobierno hubiera reducido el déficit, ahora tendría más liquidez.
Past result (B1 Unit 35): si + hubiera/hubiese + participle, habría + participle
Si hubieran aprobado el ajuste en marzo, habrían evitado la crisis ese año.

items.spanish: Si el banco central hubiera actuado antes, hoy las hipotecas serían más asequibles.
items.english: If the central bank had acted earlier, mortgages would be more affordable today.

items.spanish: Si no hubiéramos aumentado los impuestos el año pasado, ahora el déficit sería mayor.
items.english: If we had not raised taxes last year, the deficit would be larger now.

items.spanish: Si la empresa hubiera protegido sus ingresos, hoy contaría con suficiente liquidez.
items.english: If the company had protected its revenue, it would have enough liquidity today.

items.spanish: Si se hubiera aplicado el ajuste a tiempo, la presión sobre los hogares se aliviaría ahora.
items.english: If the adjustment had been applied in time, the pressure on households would ease now.

sections.content: Check the time cue in the result clause. Words like *hoy*, *ahora* and *actualmente* point to a present state and call for the simple conditional (*sería*, *tendría*), not *habría sido* or *habría tenido*. Never put the conditional (*habría*) inside the *si* clause: write *si hubiera subido*, not *si habría subido*.
